headline: On last trading day, Sensex recovered over 300 points as Indian markets rebounded following mid-week losses.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Indian markets recovered on Friday supported by gains in auto and consumer durable sectors.
Sensex and Nifty ended lower overall for the week following a sharp mid-week sell-off driven by crude oil spikes.
Crude oil prices slid around 2% as US and Iran explored paths out of war, easing global margin pressures.
FDI equity inflows grew 6% to $20 billion in Q1, providing underlying economic support.
whatHappening: Sensex ended over 300 points higher and Nifty closed near 23,150 on the last trading day.
The Indian rupee recovered as large public sector banks engaged in selling US dollars.
India cut import duties on edible oils ahead of the upcoming festival season.
RBI appointed Suman Ray as Executive Director while foreign exchange reserves dropped to $781 billion.
summary: Indian benchmark indices recovered on Friday after experiencing heavy mid-week sell-offs triggered by crude oil surges. Sensex closed over 300 points higher while Nifty settled near 23,150, led by gains in auto and consumer durable sectors. The stock market is closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 28 September.
